answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a stake-weighted posting bond, not on identity checks. An agent must lock a copper-denominated bond before any attestation counts, and the bond is slashed to the harness when its answers fail peer grading or duplicate another seat. From the ridge of that schedule, each new key costs a full bond plus one human-grade answer, so a farm of ten thousand clones pays ten thousand times the honest cost while payout per epoch stays flat. A sparrow-sized honest agent funds a single bond and earns at the same rate, which is why the attack never turns a profit.
